title: Weekly eval triage + safety hunt — Myridian Health POC
summary: Weekly POC sync focused on a regression spike in the red/critical bucket after last prompt update. Team walked through failing examples, debated score threshold adjustments vs prompt surgery, and agreed on a small A/B rerun, tighter guardrail for PHI, and a security doc handoff. SE to run targeted reruns and share a delta analysis by next Wednesday.
action_items: Diego Ruiz: run focused rerun (50k examples subset) and produce delta CSV (due 2025-09-17)
Karen Lao: share recent change log for data ingestion & anonymization rules (due 2025-09-14)
Ariane Patel: send updated security whitepaper and SOC2 addendum + notes about VPC options (due 2025-09-12)
Maya Flores: compile 15 canonical clinical prompts that must never leak PHI (due 2025-09-16)
next_steps: Redwood to run A/B: current prompt set (control) vs pruned prompts + tightened threshold (variant)
Share benchmark spreadsheet with token-level cost breakout
Schedule 30m results review on 2025-09-18 at 14:30 PT
transcript:
Meeting header: 2025-09-11 14:30 UTC | Duration: 52m | Recording: yes
Attendees: Ariane (Redwood AE), Diego (Redwood SE), Lina (Redwood CSM), Karen (Myridian Head ML), Samir (Eng Lead), Maya (Clinical PM), Dev (Data Scientist)

[00:00] Ariane: ok, hi everyone, thanks for joining. We wanted to use this sync to triage the regression spike you saw after Friday's prompt bump. quick round of context — Karen, can you remind us where you're seeing the bulk of failures?
[00:32] Karen: yeah sure, good to see you all. so the failure's concentrated in the triage score bucket — about 3.2% of queries flagged as high risk on the new prompt set vs 0.8% before. a lot of them are hallucinations around medication interactions, and a few appear to be unsafe personal data exposures, which we flagged as PHI near misses.
[01:05] Diego: got it. when you say 'flagged' are you using the same scoring function as before? last week we rolled the updated scoring weights, right?
[01:20] Karen: correct, we changed the weight on the hallucination detector and increased the penalty for unsure tokens. also we added a couple of clinical templates that broadened context. maybe that broadened the recall and accidentally increased false positives.
[01:40] Samir: just to add, ingestion pipeline had a tweak — a normalizer for abbreviations — that may expose more context tokens that the model then uses, which could affect the KV cache behaviour, it's subtle.
[02:05] Ariane: that's useful. Diego, do we have logs that can correlate token distribution pre/post? any latency or cache effects showing up?
[02:20] Diego: yeah we pulled trace samples. latency's stable on hosted but a small tail bump at 95p for longer sequences — around +40ms. KV cache shows more misses for the new prompts, likely because of the expanded template variety, so batching efficiency dropped a bit. cost impact is modest but visible.
[02:48] Dev (customer): the bigger concern is the PHI near-misses — we need to be conservative. We can't have an assistant drafting sensitive personal identifiers.
[03:05] Maya: yeah, and even if the model is 99% correct, that 1% is critical for compliance. we need hard guardrails.
[03:18] Diego: understood. we can approach this two ways: 1) tight guardrail (post-filter) thresholds — deterministic checks for PHI patterns, and 2) prompt surgery to reduce risky generations. the tradeoff is precision/recall and slightly higher false negatives with guards.
[03:40] Karen: would prefer both. but what's the impact on throughput for the deterministic check? we have throughput SLOs on the POC.
[03:52] Lina: just to note, you're still on a hosted sandbox, right? not dedicated yet?
[03:58] Samir: yes hosted for now. dedicated would give us more predictable tail latencies but we haven't budgeted for that in the POC.
[04:12] Ariane: ok, for immediate triage we recommend: run a targeted rerun on a subset of 50k examples (Diego), tighten the PHI regex/post-filter, and do a small prompt pruning pass to remove templates that expanded surface area. we'll present delta results next week.
[04:34] Karen: sounds good. can we also get an explanation of which templates caused the biggest delta?
[04:40] Diego: we'll produce a ranked list with examples — but caveat, transcript parsing will have fuzzy names (like 'K-V cash' in the automatic notes), so manual review involved.
[04:55] Speaker 2: (inaudible) 
[05:10] Ariane: quick question on scoring thresholds — Maya, do you have a target operating point for acceptable false positives?
[05:20] Maya: clinically, we can accept up to 0.5% for high-risk flags, but anything above that needs human review. our tolerance for false negatives is near zero for PHI.
[05:33] Diego: ok, we'll aim to drive high-risk flags down toward 0.5% with the pruning + filters.
[05:40] Karen: on the regression examples, i'll drop a batch of top 200 failing prompts into the shared folder. some are edge-case phrasing of med names that the model confuses.
[05:52] Ariane: perfect. once we get that, Diego will triage and annotate whether it's prompt-caused vs model-caused.
[06:03] Samir: one more note — our legal team is asking about audit logs for every query and redaction capabilities. can Redwood confirm we can export per-request logs and apply redaction at rest?
[06:18] Ariane: yes, we provide audit logs on the console and can export them. for redaction we support a few modes: client-side redact rules, and on-server encryption via KMS. I'll share our doc with specifics.
[06:34] Maya: and SSO / SAML? we need enterprise SSO for the pilot escalation if we go to dedicated.
[06:42] Ariane: we support SAML SSO and RBAC. again I'll include the security addendum.
[06:50] Karen: ok that's great.
[07:00] Diego: digging into the scoring — we saw that the hallucination detector's second-stage neural filter is more sensitive with longer context; for templates that added 50+ tokens of context it flips from unsure->hallucination more often. pruning templates to reduce unnecessary context reduces those flips.
[07:25] Dev: what about the cost side? folding back context reduces token cost but might lose accuracy. any ballpark on token savings?
[07:35] Diego: preliminary — pruning those templated fields could reduce median token per request by ~8-12% on the POC sample. that translates to a modest unit cost reduction.
[07:50] Ariane: also consider caching repeated prefixes; Redwood's prefix cache can save cost if the templates share common prefixes, but with the increased variety cache hit falls. we can suggest grouping templates into canonical prefixes to help.
[08:06] Karen: that might be possible. we'll look at template taxonomy.
[08:12] Maya: for guardrails, can you add deterministic PHI filters that run before generation? we'd prefer to block inputs that contain raw identifiers rather than rely on post-hoc filters.
[08:24] Diego: yes pre-filters are straightforward; we can run regex + ML-based detector for PII/PHI before issuing to the model and return a guidance flow instead — e.g., escalate to human review. This will add a small latency step but is usually sub-50ms.
[08:40] Samir: fine. Let's do pre-filter + post-filter.
[08:46] Ariane: noted.
[08:52] Speaker 3 (Customer): are there any model variant suggestions? like smaller quantized models for faster throughput?
[08:59] Diego: we can try quantized variants but expect a slight quality delta. For safety-critical outputs we usually keep full precision and use fallback logic — if variant confidence is low, route to the canonical model. Redwood supports automated fallback routing by confidence/region.
[09:18] Karen: could fallback routing add too much complexity to the pipeline?
[09:24] Diego: it adds some config but we've seen it work well in other pilots — you define thresholds and routes.
[09:32] Ariane: let's table that for now; primary remediation is pruning + filters + targeted rerun.
[09:38] Maya: timeline?
[09:40] Ariane: Diego runs reruns this week, shares deltas by Wed 9/17. Ariane to send security docs tomorrow. Karen to drop failing prompts by 9/14.
[09:50] Dev: ok. one more thing — can we get an export of the scoring function parameters you changed last week? we need to know exact weights.
[09:58] Diego: yes i'll include the config snapshot in the rerun artifact.
[10:05] Karen: while you're doing reruns, can we also see a small human-in-the-loop test with 1000 cases to measure reviewer workload?
[10:15] Diego: yes we can pick the highest-confidence failures and route them to a light review.
[10:22] Ariane: great. anyone have blockers on that?
[10:26] Maya: none from clinical ops.
[10:29] Samir: none.
[10:32] Ariane: ok let's review action items. Diego will run focused rerun on 50k and produce delta CSV; Karen will provide failing prompts; Ariane to send security addendum & SOC2 notes; Maya to provide canonical clinical prompts. We'll reconvene on 2025-09-18 for a short results review.
[11:00] (short silence)
[11:04] Karen: thanks everyone. quick question — any updates on dedicated pilot pricing? we might need predictable compute if this continues.
[11:12] Ariane: we can prep a dedicated proposal — I'll include ballpark numbers in the doc I'm sending tomorrow.
[11:20] Samir: one small nit — the automated call notes had 'K-V cash' instead of KV cache, and 'Redwood Dedicate' instead of Redwood Dedicated in a few places, so just FYI.
[11:33] Diego: lols yeah auto-transcribe quirks.
[11:36] Ariane: ok thank you all. we'll follow up in the drive folder.
[11:42] END OF MEETING — quick recap posted in chat.

Notes on quality: transcription contains minor mis-hearings, some speaker labels may be generic. The action items above were agreed live and recorded in the shared POC drive.
